# S7.3 — the generated files, the README, and CI actually green

Three things close this checkpoint, and only one of them was where the previous sessions thought
it was.

## 1. The generated files regenerate to the same bytes

```
> npm run headers   →  vercel.json ← headers.config.mjs (951 bytes)
> npm run content   →  content already normalized
> npm run editor    →  public/editor-panel.css (36170 bytes)
                       public/editor-inline.css (15999 bytes)
> git status --short →  (no change to any of the three)
```

All three are already what their sources say they should be, which is what the fleet's shared
pipeline diffs on every push. Nothing to commit here — that is the pass, not the absence of one.

## 2. CI was red on `main`, and had been for six commits

This is the finding of the session and it is the reason the checkpoint exists.

Every session before this one reported a green local battery, and every one of them was telling
the truth. `gh run list` said otherwise:

```
completed  failure  chore(conductor): s17 S7 RolledOver — Running
completed  failure  chore: drop the commit-message scratch file
completed  failure  fix(a11y): the last two are the Face's own hues, and latte is where they fail
completed  failure  chore(conductor): s16 S7 Advanced — Idle
completed  failure  chore(conductor): s16 S7.1 — handoff
completed  failure  feat(seo): the sitemap the template left behind, and a card per section
```

`# tests 103 · # pass 100 · # fail 3`, all three in `test/anonymity.test.mjs`, none of them
reproducible on the machine they were written on.

**Root cause.** `node:path`'s `basename` is platform-specific. `scripts/anonymity.mjs` used it to
read a repository's own name out of the path the run store recorded — and the store records the
paths of the machine the runs happened on, which is a Windows machine. On the Linux runner a
backslash is an ordinary character, so `basename("C:\code\conductor-site")` came back whole.
Nothing then equalled `conductor-site`, so:

- this site's own run stopped being recognised as its own, and its paths went on the forbidden
  list — which on a site whose subject is itself would report every page;
- a private repository's name was never extracted from its path at all, which is the same bug
  pointing the other way and is the one that matters.

**Fix.** `lastSegment` splits on both separators, so a path reads the same way wherever the check
runs. A new case pins all three shapes rather than trusting the platform to agree. The derived
list is byte-identical on the owner's machine before and after: 51 machine paths, 15 private
names, 4 distinctive tokens, 41 phrases.

**Proof** — `fix(ci): the store's paths are Windows paths, and the runner is not` (`d95f457`):

```
completed  success  fix(ci): the store's paths are Windows paths, and the runner is not  CI  main  27s
```

First green CI on `main` in this run.

## 3. Bug #6 — the gates that only ran on one laptop

Bug #6 said this repo's own gates never run in CI. Half of that was wrong, and the wrong half is
worth recording: the fleet's shared pipeline runs `npm run check`, and in this repo that is
`astro check && node --test`, so the unit suite **does** run in CI. That is how the platform bug
above was caught — by the machine nobody was watching, for six commits, while everyone watched
the local battery.

What is genuinely local-only is the four gates that read `dist/` or the run store. Two of them
cannot travel to a runner at all, and for good reasons that are not going to change:

- the corpus's staleness is a question only the run store answers;
- the anonymity list is *derived at check time* and deliberately never written down — writing it
  into the repository would be the leak the gate exists to prevent.

So each grew the half that can run anywhere, and each says on every green run which half it did
not do:

| new | checks | cannot check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run evidence:cited` | every key a page cites resolves against the committed corpus | whether that corpus still matches the store |
| `npm run anonymity:shapes` | a path out of a terminal, an API token, a bearer secret, a chat id, a bot token, a reference to the field notes | every derived name, token and phrase |

Neither weakens the full gate. `npm run evidence` and `npm run anonymity` are unchanged and are
still what runs before a report goes out.

`.github/workflows/gates.yml` runs `seo` and `a11y` whole, and those two halves. Its gate steps
survive each other's failure so one red does not hide three, and are skipped when the build itself
failed, because all four read `dist/`.

**Both new halves are proven red, not just green** — `docs/evidence/S7.3-ci-gates-red.txt`:

```
evidence: concepts/agent-memory.yaml: evidence.figures names "aFigureNobodyHarvested", which is
  not in the corpus. A key with no figure behind it is a claim with no evidence behind it.
EXIT=1

anonymity: 1 finding(s) in the built output.
  index.html: a home directory on someone's machine — C·······\ (9 chars)
EXIT=1
```

**Proof, on the runner** (`Gates` workflow, run 31147176178, green in 24s):

```
seo:       22 public page(s) all carry their own canonical, og:url and og:image; the sitemap
           lists exactly the 21 crawlable one(s); robots.txt disallows only [/api/, /edit, /og/];
           4 social card(s) at 1200×630 still render the text their PNGs were taken from.
a11y:      22 readable page(s) each carry a lang, one identified <main>, a working skip link as
           their first link, and header/nav/footer landmarks; 289 control(s) have an accessible
           name; no page reorders the tab order.
evidence:  every key cited by 17 content entries resolves against the committed corpus.json.
anonymity: 42 built files carry none of 8 secret shapes.
```

## 4. The README

Rewritten from the placeholder. The "under construction" block is gone — the site is built — and
what replaces it is the live URL, the rule that shapes everything, a table of the six gates with
what each answers and where each runs, and why there are two workflows rather than one.

## The battery, on the tree as inherited and at the end

`docs/evidence/S7.3-battery-inherited.txt` — every gate green before any edit, which is the QA
verdict on session 17: **no findings against what it claimed**. Its work stands; what it did not
know was that the machine it never looked at was red.

`docs/evidence/S7.3-battery.txt` — the same battery at the end of this session, plus the two new
halves and the state of both workflows on `main`.

## Filed, not fixed

**Bug #8:** there is no favicon. `public/` ships none of `favicon.svg`, `icon.svg`, `favicon.png`
or `favicon.ico`, and `Base.astro` links no icon, so every tab shows the browser's blank glyph and
sitekit warns on every build that the editor's webmanifest has no icons. It is a shipping defect
on the Ship stage, but the mark itself is a design decision, and S7.4 is where the owner looks at
the front page.
